messages.subject: heat map on Scatter plot
parts:
Hi All,

I am new to R programming.

I need your help to create heat map on scatter plot. I have 3 dimensions dim1, dim2 and Volume.

So data of dim1 and dim2 used to created scatter plot and I want to use volume for color shading of heat map on scatter plot.

I am using stat_density2d (Half success) by the color shading is on the basis of number of points in the region.

But I want the color shading is done on the basis of volume.

If anyone can guide/suggest me with package or function. I am ready debug and experiment.

Thanks in advance.

AFAIK, you need a matrix in order to do a heat map. So, you need to create a matrix of zeros and set only the values in your data that differ from zero.

I hope this is clear.

messages.author: dd68a26ecdacedb8
messages.subject: Re: heat map on Scatter plot
parts:
Try using geom_tile().

You're right that stat_density2d() will color by count.

Here is an example. Shading is based on the value of the Volume measure as you need:

require(ggplot2)
# experiment using 10 to show that shade is on value, not on count.
measure <- c(sample.int(10, size=1000, replace=TRUE))
x <- sample(LETTERS[3:12], 1000, replace=TRUE)
y <- sample(LETTERS[3:12], 1000, replace=TRUE)
DF <- as.data.frame(cbind(x, y, measure), row.names=FALSE)
DF$measure <- as.integer(DF$measure) # to control the data type
names(DF) <- c("dim1", "dim2", "Volume")
str(DF)
myPlot <- ggplot(DF, aes(x=dim1, y=dim2, fill=DF$Volume))
myPlot <- myPlot + geom_tile()
myPlot <- myPlot + scale_fill_gradient(low="yellow", high="red")
myPlot  # there are different ways to build and print the plot, this is just one way.
rm(myPlot)  # destroy object each time prior to trying different options

This is crude and the list of variations are numerous. It should get you going.

-Phil
